Paragraph: When the giant eagle Jatayu witnessed Sita being forcibly carried away by Ravana, he did not hesitate despite his old age. Engaging the powerful demon king in battle to protect Sita, Jatayu fought bravely until his wings were severed. Mortally wounded, he held onto life long enough to inform Rama of Sita's kidnapper, earning Rama's deepest gratitude and divine blessings.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Witnessing injustice, confronting overwhelming odds, fear of death, and feeling powerless due to age.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Jatayu acts courageously to protect another, showing that moral duty matters more than personal safety or victory.
Outcome/Resolution: Jatayu finds dignity and meaning in his heroic sacrifice, receiving supreme spiritual liberation from Rama.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Fear: Conquering fear of injury or death

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Paropkara (Selfless service to protect the vulnerable)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Jatayu demonstrates ultimate courage and selflessness, sacrificing his life to defend righteousness.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Highlights value-driven courage, overcoming bystander apathy, and finding purpose in selfless action.
